utterances.text: Yes, if the subject described a number of people who committed crimes in the camp, the proper procedure is to say, "OK, we have a line up for each of these persons you describe. First, we take this person that you describe as being there and there or doing this or that. Now here we have a lineup. See whether this particular person that you describe is in this lineup or not". Then the other elements of the instruction. So there is no uncertainty whom of all the people that witnesses might have seen in the camp is to be expected in the lineup.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would it be helpful for the Court to know whether the foils in the identity test were chosen after the descriptions were obtained from the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would say that the proper time order is not so relevant as long as the foils, sort of, fit these descriptions. I think if you first get the description and then choose the foils, it is more likely that you will get the correct foils, but it might have happened that you first get the foils and then the descriptions and that the foils happen to fit those descriptions. It just is a matter of practicality, I would say. I would do it in the one order, not in the other, but if you did it in the other order, that does not mean it went wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would it be helpful for the Court to know in which order the photos were shown to the witnesses or the arrangement of the photos as they were shown, not only to those witnesses who have been here in Court, but also those who were interviewed but not called as a witness in Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in principle, if you do a sequential presentation to more than one witness, you must vary the order. Usually, the order is determined by some sort of randomized mechanism, so that, in principle, the picture of the accused can appear in any position in the sequence. It would not be such a good idea to use only one position, for instance, because then if there is any contact among witnesses, they might communicate, say, which number they had recognised. So, if it were only for that reason, it is a good idea to always vary the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would it be helpful for the Court to know the ethnic background or the background, such as, from which countries the foils came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it would be relevant only with respect to this little proviso that I have mentioned. In general, I think that, say, the two tests that we apply generally sort of can assure you that the foils were well chosen, but there is this slight problem that in order to really draw strong conclusions from our research in Belgrade it would be better to know where these people actually came from. But that is only a proviso that I would attach, want to attach to it. I have myself no really strong doubts that something went wrong with the choice of the foils.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It would eliminate a shadow of a doubt, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure, we cannot know that for sure. There would have been a way to know that for sure by just organising it the proper way before showing the spread to witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would it be helpful for the Court to know whether these identification tests have been administered by officers who did not know which person in the photospread is the suspect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have been helpful if they had not known.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It would of course not ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we already know that in fact they did know. So, I do not quite understand your question. I think it is obvious that the investigators knew who the accused was in the photospread.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Also here to exclude any shadow of doubt, should it be helpful to the Court to know whether they knew or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure, I think they must know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would it be helpful for the Court whether the preparation and the conduct of the identification has been recorded, for example, by a video or by audio tape or by a stenographic transcript, would that be helpful, perhaps supplemented with a time log, if any were available, would that be helpful for the Court to have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it were available I think it would be extremely instructive to the Court to be able to see how the procedures actually went, because some of the problems that I have mentioned are entirely hypothetical, that it might have happened but we do not know whether it happened. If all those problems can be excluded, that would be extremely helpful to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I take it then it would be helpful to the Court too if, from those kinds of records, it would show that the recognition of Mr. Tadic had been pronounced only after a considerable time, if that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. All these elements in the procedure I think, in as far as they are not known now, could better be known to the Court in one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Wagenaar, much earlier Professor Wladimiroff asked you some questions about the history of your involvement in this matter, both with the Prosecution and the Defence. You mentioned something about the adversarial system and your understanding initially of what your role might be in the case. At that time you also understood that the Defence would, in all probability, be obtaining the services of an expert colleague in your field, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I know is that the Prosecution was the first to contact me about this case, and immediately I asked what my exact position would be because this Court is not like a Dutch court, so my position would be different from what I was used to. I expressed my preference for being appointed by the Court just in the way as I am used to in the Netherlands, but I understood also at that time that that was not the nature of our contact. It was a contact between the Prosecution and me, and we agreed that unless there was a decision that I could act as a witness for the Court or a decision that I could serve both parties equally, I would only have contact with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was your ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What the Defence would do was not the content of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. Is it not true that we discussed, at least in passing, the likelihood that the Defence would get an expert and that is the way the matter would proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was in case I could not equally help the Defence, it would be rather likely that then the Defence would seek the assistance of another expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In fact, you subsequently discovered the Defence had contacted a colleague of yours in Maastricht?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At some later time apparently that arrangement was not satisfactory and then the Defence contacted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no knowledge whether it was satisfactory. I only experienced that they contacted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was further your understanding that all reports that you produced, all tests that you conducted, would be turned over to the Defence? We had that clear understanding, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had that agreement. Let me be explicit about this. From my side that was a condition for working for the Prosecution. I am simply not used to working for one side in a trial and letting that side decide whether they would present something in court if they like it, and not present it in court if they do not like it. That is not what I am used to and that is not what I would like to happen. So I stated explicitly as a condition I am prepared to work for the Prosecution and for the Prosecution only, but under the condition that if I produce something it should also be made known to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So in responding to Mr. Wladimiroff's questions about the nature of your contact and relationship with the Prosecution, you were not attempting to suggest in any way that there was something underhanded going on between you and the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at all. You only got there first I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I understand your direct testimony correctly, you were in contact with the Defence from about October of last year, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must say I should look at my calendar to find out the proper date, but it is quite possible that that is the correct date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was interested in that, because I noted that in various portions of your testimony you indicated that there were parts of the procedure with which the transcripts did not familiarise you or provide you with sufficient information to determine exactly what you thought you might need to know. Did you indicate to the Defence that these are matters that should be taken up with the witnesses who participated in these procedures, so that that information could be elicited for your benefit so you could express a view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not because to my understanding, well, the date of my report about those parts of the record is 10th October which is very recently. I received those documents not much before that date. By that date the interrogations of those witnesses had come to an end. So it really would not have helped if, say, I had received documents halfway through the interview of witnesses. I could have suggested to one party or the other, "Listen, there are a number of things that I would like to know, maybe you can ask the next witnesses about these things", but that was not the situation when I received the documents. All the witnesses, as far as I know, had been heard and that part of the trial had been concluded. I must maybe add for your clarification, which is just a matter of fact and I cannot help it, I would wish it were otherwise but it is not, there is no way I could combine a complete reading of the trial records with my job as a professor of psychology in Leiden. I have to satisfy myself with just a small part. It is not my habit to read only part of the records. It is my habit it read all of it, but in this case it is simply not humanly possible, definitely not within the time that was given to me. So I have made that clear restriction. This is what I have read. It is in my letter. I was assured that those are the pages that refer to identification and that there are no other pages. If I am wrong I am prepared to read more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just so it is understood, when did you receive documents for review for purposes of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Wladimiroff could tell you the exact date. Wait a minute. It is not mentioned in my letter. I might have with me the letter in which it was offered, but it was not long before. I do not think I have the letter with me. I think I must fail the answer, but probably it is something like two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before you responded with the letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. I am not certain of the answer. I have to look it up in our sort of letter book in which it is recorded when letters are received.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In any event, it was a relatively short time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Relatively short time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long before that was it that you discussed for the first time in any way the issues of identification procedures with the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think at the time that you mentioned our first contact you located that, what did you say, in -- I am not quite sure, I think you said March 1996?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, this is your first discussion with the Defence about these issues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The only discussion I had with the Defence, including the first, was only on the identification. I am not an expert on any other aspect of this trial. So all our discussions, and there were not many, including the first, was on identification, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At that time did you provide them with a copy of your book which includes the 50 rules you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think they had it in their possession already.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Doctor, I understand what you have just indicated about the length of time you had to review these records and transcripts. Let me ask you then about a matter that was discussed at some length during your direct testimony, and that is the test or identification test or photospread administered to the witness Draguna Jaskic. Do you remember the discussion about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the witness who changed her testimony in the second account, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, you say change her testimony in the second account, was she shown the photospread twice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I think I described that I am not completely aware of what exactly happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not she was shown the photospread once or twice or more times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me first make sure we are talking about the same witness, that was my counter question. These names are terribly confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please satisfy yourself about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I have the same documents that you have with the names and the abstracts. In the document that was given to you today, which is a short listing of the pages that were given to me, I think the witness with whom there was a small problem is listed between No. 58 and 60 with no number attached to her. There her name is mentioned as Draguna Jaskic. It appears on page 2952. That is the witness you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We are at least talking about the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you can keep handy those pages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Identification is always a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understood you to say that you were unaware of whether or not she had participated in more than one photospread?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am not completely certain what the procedure was that was applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That question was rather clearly addressed in the portions of the transcript which you received, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have those pages starting at 2952.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Perhaps you want to take a look at page 2969.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 2969, yes, I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did you interpret the questions and answers when they came to you the second time: "Did they have photographs with them again?" Answer "No". So you did not look at another book of photographs after that first time?" Answer "No"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I read that, but I did not understand how she came about to give a second statement about whom she had recognised. Apparently, there is a second visit, or maybe it was -- it says at line 6, "When they visited you again and said 'why did you not say'?", there is a riddle there because apparently there is a second visit. Mr. Kay seems to imply there that the investigator already knows that she did not say something, although she knew, and my question is how did the investigator know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let us see if we can address that question then. Let me ask you first about forms of recognition, because I noted in particular that you said that this witness did not express any recognition, did not recognise and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that I think. She did not express it and then the rule is you should count her as someone who did not identify.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I think one of the quotes you had was "could not recognise" but let us not quibble about that. One of the forms of recognition, or one of the expressions of recognition, can be of course the simple statement, "I recognise that person as the one who did such and such", correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is also true to say that not all expressions of recognition need to be verbal. For example, someone can point in response to a question and that is also an indication of recognition. I take it would also be true that there are some reactions which are as demonstrative of recognition as pointing or speaking. For example, if someone encountered someone from whom they had great reason to fear and reacted by running from the room screaming in tears, that certainly might also be an expression of recognition, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, now you come on very difficult ground, because if you accept all sorts of emotional, expression of emotions as recognition, then you are going to ask the investigator to interpret the behaviour of the witness. There you are on very slippery ground. Therefore, the procedure asks that the witness just says, "I indicated a number, that is the one I recognise." Points, indicates, says and no other less clear things because you would become dependent on all sorts of subjective interpretations of the investigator and you do not want that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Doctor, I appreciate you cannot ask a witness in lieu of verbal expression to have some physical reaction to the photograph or the individual to express their recognition. Of course that would not be practical. Nevertheless, that might happen, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anything might happen. So what you would expect in that case is the investigator just describes what happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right, and in that case it might not be the investigator who is interpreting what is happening. It is the investigator bringing information to the court and allowing the Court to determine what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If everything is described you can leave it to the Court to interpret it, yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You would also agree, I take it, that that can be a very persuasive expression of one's recognition, a very sincere expression of one's recognition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What can be a very sincere expression?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: An involuntary physical reaction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Running from the room and screaming?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Breaking out into a sweat, whatever kinds of physical expressions might result.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say breaking out into a sweat is exactly the thing I would have doubts about, because that is not easy to see, not always to easy to see and it is not always easy to attribute it just to recognition. It can be related to almost anything. So, no, I think when I say that there ought to be strict and clear procedures, some of the procedures relate to how the recognition is expressed. Some of the expressions are perfectly acceptable and clear and do not need to be quibbled with. Another thing, because they are doubtful and subject to personal interpretation which cannot be redone or undone by the Court because the Court cannot verify whether the investigator saw a sweat, I would say that is a less desirable procedure. I think to such a situation you ought to apply one of the rules that was formulated, which is if you can justify why by necessity you had to do it this way, I could not follow, say, the optimum procedure, maybe the Court should accept that. But if it cannot be justified, then I would not encourage investigators to do it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Doctor, the question was not intended to be, and I apologise if it seemed to be, a question which asked you to comment on the best possible procedure under those circumstances. I simply wanted to know whether you acknowledge that a recognition could be expressed in a variety of ways including a physical reaction? I think you agree with that, is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I think witnesses can do that. I do not want to have said that that should be acceptable as a procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not as a procedure. You should focus on the existence of a recognition or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rather you should instruct witnesses not to express it in other ways than by saying it and pointing at the right picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I think I understood that from your earlier testimony as well. Let me ask you one more question. Is it also possible, in your view, that an individual who sees a photograph or a person who elicits great fear reacts to that fear by trying to distance himself or herself from the situation and verbally expressing or denying that recognition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sure, I think that is perfectly possible. I do not think such a person makes a great witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You read the full transcript of Mrs. Jaskic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, you read the pages you were given that included page 2977?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would it be helpful if I tell you which pages I have?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I actually have a list of that I believe so I can accompany you with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had 53, 2953, 54, 55, then jumping to 62, then 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69 and that is the end. I do not know which proportion of the whole testimony that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On page 2977 ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 2977, I did not have that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were not provided with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Sure, OK, that is the next testimony. Right. That is by Mr. Paepen I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is right. The reaction that Mrs. Jaskic had at the time she viewed the photospread was described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think you have refer to me to the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Doctor, I am referring to lines 27 through 32.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It seems you did not recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. No, I recall that. I do not know exactly what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right, you do not know what it means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This witness brought that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sure but I do not know whether ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is for the Court to determine exactly what that means, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, if your suggestion is that one can conclude from that piece that obviously she recognised, I cannot conclude that. I can only see that she behaved in this way and then said "Go on". If you just stick to the rules it would say, so, that is not a recognition because then she should have said "That's him" and maybe run screaming from the room, but "Go on" sort of means that she would want to have a look at the other pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So it is not a recognition under the rules?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under proper rules I would say do not count that as recognition. It is risky. You do not know exactly what happens, why she made that. If I may add, it is quite probably -- no, not probably. I should correct it. It is possible that the uncertainty of the situation has led to this. If her task was to recognise the one person she had mentioned, I do not know whether she had mentioned the name Tadic, I think she did, if she had been asked, "Well, that one person, is he in this file or not?" and she recognised him, she might have said here, "That's him, stop". If she was under the allusion that she might see more people whom she had met in the camp, it could it could have been possible for her to say after recognising one, "Go on" expecting some more, you see. The unclarity or maybe the possible impropriety of the procedure may have led to this difficulty. I would say good procedures avoid also interpretation problems. So, I do not even know what the "Go on" means. Does she mean, "I am not sure whether it is him. Go on, maybe we get a better picture of him". Or does she mean, "Go on, maybe there are other criminals that I might also recognise." It is sort of very difficult to interpret what this all means and proper procedures avoid such difficulties.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Actually, as I recall the testimony, she did not testify that she had recognised him in a camp, but hat she recognised him in Jaskici. It has been months since we heard this testimony, but that is my memory. The reason I suggest this to you is, would it have been helpful for you to have read her testimony in full to have understood at least what she testified to, what were the circumstances, how it affected her, to better understand her reaction? I have had the advantages of listening to that some time ago. I have not read it since but I remember it. Would that have helped you and would possibly you have formed a different opinion as to what she meant when she reacted that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is thinkable that that would have helped me to help you understand what she meant, but I do not think it is in my field of expertise to help you what she meant. My field of expertise is procedure. If you would ask me to look at it again and help you explain what she means, I would be very hesitant to be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We have a very difficult job and I think it belongs to us, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I appreciate that. You need all the help you can. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Tieger. I may have misremembered but that is my memory and that is why I wanted to ask it. It is now 5.30. So we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day).

(which may be did not happen, but one cannot be completely sure)
(The Court adjourned for a short time)
